  • Death Is Irrelevant is the card in question, and this eight-mana enchantment is a must-have for artifact creature decks, especially when most builds in the archetype can afford the huge mana cost long before turn eight.
  • The question, however, is why the price has suddenly spiked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Magic: The Gathering card prices are forever on the move, but given how weak the Star Trek set has been, we didn't expect to see a card from the set randomly spike by over 200% overnight.

Death Is Irrelevant is the card in question, and this eight-mana enchantment is a must-have for artifact creature decks, especially when most builds in the archetype can afford the huge mana cost long before turn eight.

The question, however, is why the price has suddenly spiked. We'd known about the card for some time, and the preview window made it clear it would be huge for artifact creature decks, but its price crashed along with the rest of the Star Trek set upon release.

It's taken almost three weeks for the price to spike, but is it a long-term move, or can we expect it to crash again in a few days?

Industry observers note that on Monday, November 23, the average price of the Death Is Irrelevant LCARS variant was $13.99, but on Tuesday, November 24, this shot up to $44.39. The market price hasn't moved with it (yet), but listings across multiple marketplaces, including TCGplayer, show that the average listing price across all variants is rising.

Some listings still remain close to the original price, but many have also been bought up quite quickly, leaving the higher-priced listing as the only alternative.

It's worth noting, however, that a lot of the increased prices across all three variants of this card are being put up by one seller on TCGplayer, which either points to market manipulation attempts to raise the market value of the card and make it appear more desirable and valuable than it is, or they have the inside track on upcoming demand and are preparing for the incoming wave by raising their prices in anticipation.

In short, we wouldn't advise jumping on the card if you find listings online, but if you've opened a copy or two in your Star Trek packs, it's worth setting them aside to see what happens next.

While the odd Star Trek card is seeing a spike in value, not nearly enough is happening across the set to change perceptions of this Universes Beyond product.

Industry observers note that excluding the signed headliner cards, which aren't really considered valuable for Magic purposes, the most valuable card in the set appears to be the showcase surge foil variant of Captain Jean-Luc Picard at $201.16. There are only four other cards with a value over $100 in the set, a quite unprecedented scenario for a newly introduced Magic set.

It's raised a lot of questions about the viability of Star Trek as a Universes Beyond property and called for greater scrutiny of properties selected for future Universes Beyond sets. Players have put forward numerous reasons why Star Trek didn't work as a Magic set, from its cultural relevance to the lack of focus on just one aspect of the property, but all we can hope now is that Wizards has learned its lesson and future Universes Beyond sets are greatly improved.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is finally here, and it's packed full of exciting, chills-inducing moments.
  • In all the fun, though, you might have missed a few details that jumped out at us.
  • It has been revealed that so, for our deep dive, head to the below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's almost time. The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is finally here, and it's packed full of exciting, chills-inducing moments.

In all the fun, though, you might have missed a few details that jumped out at us. That's where we come in. Below, we've broken down the 14 biggest details in the new Avengers: Doomsday trailer that you might have overlooked, so you can get fully up to speed on the Marvel Phase 6 movie.

It has been revealed that so, for our deep dive, head to the below. Afterwards, be sure to check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies for everything else that's on the way.

The main takeaway from the trailer is that Steve Rogers is well and truly back. He returns to action with Earth's Mightiest Heroes after a visit from the Fantastic Four. However, there's a lot to unpack here. For one thing, there appear to be two different timelines, identifiable by Steve having short hair in one, and longer hair and a bear in the other (plus, Peggy Carter goes from a vintage, period-appropriate look to a more modern style). It's also revealed that their son is much older than the baby we were introduced to in the first Doomsday teaser. If that wasn't enough, there's the question of what Loki visited Steve and Peggy for, if the Fantastic Four arrive to collect him later. Also, it's now clearer than ever that Steve going back to live with Peggy is indeed the catalyst for the film's plot.

Thor seems to give the assembled heroes in Avengers Tower a rousing speech that we hear just a snippet of. He urges them to put their differences aside, and he also acknowledges that he doesn't really know who everyone is. This feels like Marvel slyly poking fun at itself for the oversaturation of the past few years – and it also seems to be the "heroes finally stop bickering to come together" beat of the story.

Recent findings suggest that the end of the trailer is enough to give even the most jaded of viewers chills. For the first time, we see the X-Men and the Avengers unite properly against Doctor Doom as the score blasts, in what looks to be the film's version of the "Avengers! Assemble" moment from Endgame.

Enough about the heroes: Doctor Doom doesn't feature heavily in the upcoming trailer, but we do get an ominous glimpse of him flanked by his witchy backup. The VisionQuest post-credits scene revealed that one of these is none other than a freshly-resurrected Scarlet Witch, too.

In a recent development, we finally get to hear Cyclops say "to me, my X-Men!" in the fight at the X-Mansion. This is the first time the famous catchphrase has been noted in the MCU by an X-Men member.

We know the plot will feature incursions, and in this trailer we see two worlds looking as if they're about to crash into Earth. Though, which worlds exactly are on the collision course remains to be seen.

The Avengers Tower has a fancy latest entrance, which allows the Fantastic Four's ship to land inside the logo. Is this an upgrade that arrived after the Thunderbolts post-credits scene brought Marvel's First Family to the main timeline?

Industry observers note that tony Stark himself doesn't feature in the trailer, but his memorial does. The poignant Avengers: Endgame moment that saw his Arc Reactor floating in the water is shown again in the Doomsday trailer, when Steve is talking about the events of that movie. Considering we still don't know why Robert Downey Jr. is playing Doctor Doom, this feels like a significant tease.

According to recent reports, we know the Avengers and X-Men will come to blows, but a split second moment in the final trailer shows Sam Wilson, AKA Captain America, and Cyclops fighting it out. Uh oh….

In another brief moment, we see Steve Rogers and Bucky Barnes joyfully embracing while Sam Wilson watches on, looking equally pleased. It's a nice reunion for the three best buds.

Bob, AKA Sentry, hasn't had a major presence in the marketing so far, but he can be seen sitting in the background of Avengers Tower.

Thor uses his yellow lightning powers in the trailer, which have been teased in posters so far. This could be the Odinforce, an incredibly strong power.

News of Kate Bishop's return broke ahead of the trailer, but we get our first look at her in the film in the latest footage. It's a fleeting glimpse, however, and how she might be involved is anyone's guess.

In a recent development, we also get our first look at Ant-Man's daughter, Cassie Lang, in the new trailer. Like the Kate Bishop moment, it's very brief, but she doesn't look very happy.

Recent findings suggest that avengers: Doomsday arrives on December 16 in the UK and December 18 in the US. In the meantime, check out our guide on watching the Marvel movies in order to catch up with a marathon.

You're probably describing at least half of the horror genre when you list Silent Hill and Fatal Frame as two of your main inspirations, but Ugly Within has cut through the crowded space with a reveal at The Horror Game Awards 2026.

It is in development for PS5, Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with no release window confirmed yet. Catch it in action in the trailer above.

It has been revealed that you play as two characters: Shu, a boy who can see into the past, and Reiko, an exorcist. It sounds like you'll be looking into a family history and confronting the ghost that has haunted it. Shu is a more stealthy character who avoids the supernatural and solves puzzles, while Reiko confronts the ghosts and exorcises them.

Shu and Reiko face the horrors of the Kamata estate in very different ways. Shu survives by staying unseen, moving through the house in silence and piecing together its secrets through visions of what once happened within its walls. Reiko meets the darkness head-on, confronting the entities that haunt the estate and driving them out through exorcism. But Shu's gift comes with a cruel limit: his visions reveal what happened to the people who came before, yet nothing he sees can be undone.

Recent findings suggest that there is a touch of jank to the footage released so far, but the production quality overall appears to be really quite high. A lot like Perceptum, I think this one of the indie horror titles you need to keep an eye on.

Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

📅 15 May 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • Industry observers note that the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving newly introduced content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

Industry observers note that the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

Industry observers note that the message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a upcoming automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very promptly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.

In a recent development, follow-up tests showed that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed. The experts at Digital Foundry have now weighed in on this, and they've come to pretty much the same conclusion - that it's not really a viable way to play.

Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:.

Industry observers note that "Unfortunately, while the unlock glitch is academically interesting, it doesn't provide a huge improvement to responsiveness. Our capture tools show frame-rates in the 30fps to 40fps range on Series X, with Rich recording an average frame-rate of 36fps during the first hour of the game.".

The sped-up gameplay is also mentioned, described as an "oddity" that "makes the game inconsistent and harder to control", although this is mentioned to be more likely a result of the bug rather than GTA 6's code being tied to frame rate.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, there's one specific advantage that's brought up as part of this glitch, which is that it reduces the game's input lag. Digital Foundry's tests showed that the game provided around 170ms of lag at the 30FPS mark, while a 40FPS scene dropped it to around 120ms. However, the varied frame rates are remarked to provide an "unsettling" feel overall, and one that probably outweighs the smoother feel during specific 30FPS+ moments.

The outlet indicates that a 40FPS mode when using a VRR supported display "could still make sense" on Xbox Series X, but "the game's CPU limits remain the largest barrier against such a mode" due to occasions where GTA 6 can't even reach 30FPS as things stand, while it might also require extra work such as implementing FSR upscaling tech.

It has been revealed that "A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense, but it's far from an open-and-shut case to say that such a mode would be an improvement overall against the current 30fps cap. It might also require extra work, such as integrated FSR 4 on Series X in service of a higher frame-rate when GPU limited, which wouldn't be the work of a moment. Finally, it looks like a 60fps mode is fundamentally unachievable on current console hardware.".

It has been revealed that who knows whether Rockstar Games will be able to put in the work to provide a 40FPS mode in the future, but we're going to bet they'll stick with 30FPS and simply aim for 60FPS when Xbox Project Helix and the PS6 hit the market. They've got plenty of work to do with the PC version of GTA 6, not to mention the GTA Online version of the game that's surely in the works, so pushing to hit 40FPS on current-gen consoles seems unlikely.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Avengers: Doomsday final trailer is here, and it's all about Steve Rogers – from his personal sacrifice of leaving behind Peggy and their son, through to joining Thor and the OG X-Men in a battle against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

But the first minute or so of the trailer is riddled with inconsistencies about the one-time Captain America – and I think it's telling us more than it's letting on.

Sources indicate that the opening seconds of the Doomsday trailer again reveals the moment Steve and Peggy reunite in Endgame. Then, it has a montage of a clean-shaven Steve packing away his Captain America gear, holding his baby boy, and later teaching him how to ride a bike.

But the Steve we have seen so far – both in this trailer and elsewhere – reveals him with longer hair and a beard, even right up to when the Fantastic Four rock up outside his doorstep.

Apart from telling us that Doomsday picks up with Steve and Peggy having a teenage son sometime in the early 1960s, it appears that the Fantastic Four aren't crossing the multiverse to meet him.

Instead, my theory is that Steve actually ended up visiting Peggy on Fantastic Four's Earth-828, a decision that caused much of the multiverse to collapse upon itself – and put Steve in Doom's sights.

"We didn't know those choices would have consequences," Steve Rogers notes of the decision to travel through time in Avengers: Endgame to reclaim the Infinity Stones and use them against Thanos in the Battle for Earth.

Simply put, Steve Rogers' past and present actions are catching up to him. He shouldn't have gone back through time (on either occasion), he is potentially on the wrong Earth, and he has a son that should never have existed.

So, Avengers: Endgame's final dance could actually be the opening salvo to the universe ending – and caused the incursions (such as the worlds appearing in the sky in one Doomsday trailer moment) that is leading to the collapse of the universe. Good job, Steve.

Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 14 in the UK and December 16 in the US.

  • Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.
  • Sources indicate that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games.
  • The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

Sources indicate that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the organization's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

In a recent development, we're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously.
  • But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski.
  • In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!".

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

According to recent reports, offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

It has been revealed that outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The significant question going into Black Friday this year is how far the RAM crisis will affect the deals. Dell's response to this is to ask "what crisis?" as it's introduced its own Black Friday deals on a range of its Alienware products, and there are some pretty massive discounts on gaming laptops.

According to recent reports, any purchase on Dell's Black Friday site gets you a range of bonuses, but they stack best with a deal cutting $900 off the Alienware 16 Aurora, on certain configurations. This lets you pick up a laptop with a great-looking display, Intel Core processor and specs designed for mid-range gaming, all at a bargain price.

It has been revealed that the Alienware 16 Aurora with an RTX 5050, 16GB memory and 512GB storage is best discounted, with $900 off. Models with a better graphics card, more memory or extra storage are also discounted to varying degrees, but this reduction saves the most money.

In a recent development, with any purchase from Dell's website over Black Friday, you get certain perks. The brand's offering 30% off software tools like McAfee or Microsoft 365, as well as a multi-buy discount on years of its Alienware Elite Care support service. The best deal, though, is that you get 25 free Xbox games; the brand hasn't listed what they are, but notes they have a $500 value.

Industry observers note that the version of Alienware 16 Aurora with the biggest discount, listed above, is also the weakest. Its Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050 is the lowest-end member of the brand's most recent graphics card line-up, and the 16GB RAM isn't enough for the most advanced games either.

In a recent development, so this laptop is best for mid-range or low-end games, whether that's new indie titles, older games or the big names of yesteryear at their lowest graphics options. That's not to criticize the laptop, and many people won't need anything stronger than that.

The Alienware 16 Aurora also comes in models with the 4050, 5060 and 5070, and there are discounts on at least one version with each, but the savings aren't as good.

We've reviewed the Alienware 16X Aurora laptop, which is a more advanced model than the one listed above, but with a much higher price.

Several 16X Aurora models are discounted by up to $400, but given that it's already a more expensive option than the 16, that means the deal prices are at least $1,000 more than the reduced 16.

Recent findings suggest that if you've got the budget for the Alienware 16X Aurora, you'll notice the difference when you're playing games, so it might seem like a better buy. But that price is a lot higher.

It's worth asking if you need this high-spec laptop. If you don't plan to play any GPU-intensive games, an RTX 5050 might be enough. And if you want a little more power, it may be more economical to find a more powerful 16 Aurora, rather than add the 'X'.

#166368. Breaking: How to find the serial killer in GTA 6

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1418 w)

Breaking: How to find the serial killer in GTA 6

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there's a GTA 6 serial killer to find once you reach Chapter 2.
  • It has been revealed that the Missing Person GTA 6 mission can be started in GTA 6 Chapter 2 as Lucia (or as Jason once you unlock the ability to switch characters in GTA 6).
  • Sources indicate that once inside, turn left and walk straight, then enter the small room with the red light on your right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's a GTA 6 serial killer to find once you reach Chapter 2. You may have noticed three missing person posters in the Starlet Motel reception - three Port Gellhorn tourists went missing over 20 years ago, yet no one has been able to locate them. However, the posters include a tip line number you can ring, should you happen to find the missing people. This GTA 6 side mission is easy to miss, but finding all three missing tourists leads you to a deranged serial killer – a bit like in the Red Dead Redemption 2 Killer Clue mystery. However, whether you decide to hunt down the killer alone or with your partner has consequences on how this mission plays out.

It has been revealed that the Missing Person GTA 6 mission can be started in GTA 6 Chapter 2 as Lucia (or as Jason once you unlock the ability to switch characters in GTA 6). To start this GTA 6 mission go to the bunker-like warehouse slightly north-east of Moses' garage in Port Gellhorn. It's a long dome building covered in overgrown foliage and graffiti with a shutter on its front – you can see it if you look right from the front of Moses' garage. If you try to break in through the shutter, the shutter immediately drops as soon as you try to lift it. Instead, go to the north-east side of the building and you'll find a space you can crawl through to get in.

Sources indicate that once inside, turn left and walk straight, then enter the small room with the red light on your right. Go through this room and into the next one; it appears to be a trophy room, inside which you'll find two missing posters on the right-hand wall and an armchair facing a row of lockers. Each locker contains creepy framed photographs of the missing tourists from the posters and what appears to be their belongings. Examine each of the three sets of photographs carefully as the images hint where you'll find that missing person.

Below, I've broken down where you can find each of the three missing people in GTA 6, with a more detailed breakdown available in the sections which follow.

Susanne Keeble's photographs are found in the first locker in the creepy building's trophy room. The first photo appears to show her pink car outside a junkyard and the second shows a close off of her car, which has the license plate "PRTTYGRL.".

Head to the Port Gellhorn Pay 'N' Spray and go behind the garage to find the junk yard (slightly south-east). At the junkyard's entrance, look left to see a "No Parking" sign, and you should spot Susanne's pink car behind it. Jump the fence and press Y/Triangle to open the trunk. You'll find Susanne's remains inside. Select Y/Triangle to report the body to the Kelly County Missing Persons Tip Line.

Recent findings suggest that patrick Murray's locker is the second one (from the left) in the trophy room. His photographs show a trailer in the shadow of a water tower and a newspaper clipping. The water tower is in north-east Port Gellhorn, so head toward there and you should see the tower's orb-shaped structure in the distance.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Sources indicate that once you arrive at the water tower, jump the fence north of it to enter a trailer park that's in its shadow – like in the photograph. Enter the accessible trailer that's closest to the tower/fence you jumped (a dog barks at the door). When you enter the trailer look at the gap in the floorboards to your right, then select Triangle/Y to examine the floorboards. Your character will lift the floorboards to find Patrick Murray's remains under the floor. Select Triangle/Y to report the body to Kelly County TIp Line, but this time, someone will answer your call.

The third and final locker contains photographs of Donald Miller, with the images taken at a lake near a snarled tree. The lake in the images is the one that is shaped like a U with a tail, right on the border between Port Gellhorn and Wild Hog Point, southwest of Port Gellhorn, just before the bridge.

Look for the tree and you'll find a submerged car next to the tree stump near it. Wade into the water and then press Y/Triangle when prompted to examine the car, revealing Donald Miller's remains in the passenger seat. Once again, press Triangle/Y on your controller to report the body.

Industry observers note that after finding the final body, you need to wait until the Kelly County TIp Line contact calls you. This can take some time and I didn't receive a call until night, after unlocking Jason as a playable character again by completing the Chapter 2 Breakfast Run mission. It appears you need access to both characters before you can progress this GTA 6 side mission.

It has been revealed that when the TIp Line contact does call, he'll tell you that he's looked into the evidence you've collected and he thinks there's another victim. He asks you to meet him back at warehouse where you found the lockers (officially called the creepy building) to discuss his findings.

How the rest of this mission plays out depends on whether you meet the contact alone or as a pair. If you go to the warehouse as a couple, completing the Missing Person mission is easier, but completing it alone is more exciting and offers the opportunity to increase your GTA 6 relationship status. Stop reading here if you want to avoid spoilers.

Head back to the creepy building in Port Gellhorn as either Jason or Lucia. Once again, crawl through the gap in the wall and follow the stranger's calls into the trophy room. When you enter the room, you'll meet the ominous Alvan West, who points you toward the end locker, where you find a photograph of Jason and Lucia. Immediately Alvan attacks you, holding a chloroform cloth to your nose and mouth. Regardless of whether you successfully struggle or not, Alvan will kidnap you.

You then switch to your partner, who receives a suspicious message asking you to meet them at an abandoned mine near the Kalaga Reservoir in Lummox County's Mount Kalaga National Park. When you arrive at the waypoint, enter the abandoned mine and follow the green lights to find your partner trapped in a wooden box weighed down with rocks. After freeing them, don't simply follow the green lights to find Alvan, but use focus mode to follow his voice (struggling against him when he ambushes you).

In a recent development, you eventually fall out of a tunnel and Alvan ambushes you again. Fend him off and then chase him to the dead end that sits over a huge drop. Alvan begins begging for his life, but you must not listen to his pleas. If you don't shoot him immediately he grabs a pickaxe from behind a crate and whacks you in the stomach, killing you instantly. The only option you have is to kill Alvan. His body will fall off the wooden ledge and into the darkness below.

Sources indicate that with Alvan dead, return to your partner and you'll head back to the motel. Whoever was kidnapped will not immediately be available to switch to, but if you ask them to team up and both head outside, you can then switch back to them. While you don't get a monetary reward for completing this side mission, it does improve Jason and Lucia's relationship status.

Sources indicate that make sure you have grouped up Jason and Lucia then use the crawl space to enter the creepy building again. Go to the trophy room and you'll meet Alvan. Rather than one of you being kidnapped, Jason and Lucia confront Alvan about his crimes.

A demo for ghost photography survival horror game echograph is now available for PC via Steam, developer Pappy’s Pipe Dream announced.

Here is an overview of the game, via Pappy’s Pipe Dream:.

Influenced by classics of the genre, echograph perfectly blends pulse-pounding survival horror gameplay with an intimate narrative about a generational family curse.

Recent findings suggest that players will cross the threshold into a haunting and decaying manor as Layla, the sole survivor of a dark and terrible night that claimed her entire family. Years after the incident, she returns to her familial home to uncover what really happened—and why she was the only one who survived.

As they explore a labyrinthian manor filled with secrets and environmental puzzles, players will encounter the vengeful spirits that now stalk its halls. With an occult-tinged camera as their only defense, they’ll have to engage in heart-pounding photo-based combat and careful resource management if they wish to survive the night.

Featuring a crunchy PSX-inspired aesthetic and tense isometric to first-person perspective switching gameplay, echograph delivers a stylish and highly-atmospheric take on a beloved genre.

The demo includes approximately 45-minutes of classic survival horror content from the game’s opening, and supports Japanese, Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish (Latin American & European) localization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, at the moment occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

Sources indicate that all of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Industry observers note that steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

According to recent reports, that latest patch was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of complications.

"We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the concern," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there presently looks to have been no substantial hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

Okay, you'll have to stick with me for this one because it's going to take some explaining...

It has been revealed that so, all the way back in 2023, a supposed leak on the GTAForums (please beware of potential GTA 6 spoilers if you click this link) attracted relatively little attention. At the time, there was no way to prove that any of it was legit.

The "leak" in question revealed Rockstar's schedule, with the original poster claiming that a sequel to LA Noire would be the developer's next game, after GTA 6, and it was targeting a 2030 release.

Recent findings suggest that the reason it's being brought again almost three years later — chiefly via Reddit — is because as it turns out, the leaker did get a number of details about GTA 6 correct. Most notably, they managed to provide surprisingly solid info on the game's multiple endings — and they'd obviously be quite difficult to predict without some kind of insider knowledge.

Sources indicate that to be clear, not everything in the "leak" has ended up being correct. It's a little hit and miss, but then things can change in the space of two and a half years or so; it's possible that these inaccurate details were legit at or before the time of posting.

I think the deciding factor for the believers here is that Rockstar moving on to a newly introduced LA Noire would make some sense.

Assuming it's in line with the first game, you would think that it would be a much smaller production than something like Red Dead Redemption 3 — even with the tech and engine refinements the tech giant has made with GTA 6.

Plus, there is some LA Noire DNA in both Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6; environmental and NPC interactions are key parts of Rockstar's most recent releases, and they arguably stem from LA Noire's investigative gameplay loop.

It's also worth remembering that after LA Noire's original developer Team Bondi was closed in 2011 (with Rockstar retaining the rights to LA Noire itself), its founder Brendan McNamara would go on to establish a newly introduced outfit called Video Games Deluxe.

Sources indicate that the Australian studio crafted LA Noire: The VR Case Files years later, and even took over post-launch support for GTA: The Trilogy following its incredibly shoddy launch. Video Games Deluxe was then acquired by Rockstar in 2025, and it was renamed Rockstar Australia. Hmmm.

Industry observers note that so some of this stuff seems to line up — but I don't think there's quite enough evidence here to nail the suspect. I mean, er, put your full trust in that original leak. Still, I wouldn't say no to another LA Noire.

It has been revealed that would you love to see an LA Noire sequel? Feel free to doubt all of this in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally here a good 13 years after Grand Theft Auto 5, bringing a unique male and female duo of protagonists for players to choose from with it: Lucia and Jason.

The couple certainly stands out when put beside past games' own leads, especially seeing as it shines the spotlight on a woman (yes, very old entries like the original Grand Theft Auto let you choose between female characters, too, but newer games like Rockstar's fifth have not) – and former developers like Brian Baglow, who worked on the OG GTA, think it's a breath of fresh air compared to the usual male formula.

Industry observers note that regarding the franchise's portrayal of women, Baglow tells CBC that the representation "has not been good, to put it mildly." That checks out, considering all the backlash entries as recent as GTA 5 spurred by instances of sexism and questionable themes. "I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist," he adds. "I think it's been long, long overdue.".

The ex-Rockstar dev states it's a sign of improvement on the studio's part: "I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland." And, back to the controversy past entries sparked for their representation of women (or lack thereof), like GTA 5 – Baglow describes how it's not likely the organization didn't take any note of that.

Industry observers note that "I don't think that could have passed Rockstar by, so I'm relatively sure Lucia would have been part of their intends from quite early on," he concludes. I suppose that makes sense. After all, it's been well over a decade now since Grand Theft Auto 5, giving the team plenty of time to address any long-standing feedback from fans and critics alike. The topic of women in the franchise would offer no exception there.

Breaking: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3401 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that much like the H.P.
  • In a recent development, when I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond.
  • In a recent development, I'm only somewhat correct about all this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.

In a recent development, when I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

In a recent development, I'm only somewhat correct about all this. Penguin Colony's reference points are wide-ranging and precise, with the persona of a disinterested penguin serving partly as a means of critical distance from Lovecraft, and partly, as a kind of camouflage for an extremely complex political artwork. It's easy to treat the game's critique as wholly retrospective - an alternately mocking and outraged investigation of a horror author whose bigotry is often reduced to an apologetic footnote or tinny performative disclaimer, drowned out by dread augurs of tentacles in the dark. It's a test of interpretative rigour, amongst other things, for hasty white European reviewers who might slip and slide past the more elaborate allusions into idle chat about Soulslikes.

Industry observers note that speaking to me over videocall, Origame Digital founder and director Naphtali Faulkner acknowledged the broad objective of reframing colonial cities as unearthly aberrations, cutting against cosier visions of colonised Australian land. "There's a bit of an glitch with Australian games, where they tend to be tourism pieces, sometimes," he comments. "Not in a bad way, but they do not bring up the violence of this country, in anything. They will comfortably sidestep that for a lot of reasons – one is, a lot of the families that are affected by that are still around. Is it [a non-indigenous developer's] place to tell that story? No. But also, you have this sort of 'Australiana' stuff happen quite a lot, where it's tin roofs and red dirt, that kind of look you see on a postcard.".

It has been revealed that still, Penguin Colony's "first colonial city" isn't just a response to 'Australiana'. It's also a monument to 2b2t, the ancient Minecraft "anarchy" server that is infamous for its vicious player culture, and somewhat admired for the colossal strangeness of its desecrated geography. 2b2t is an incarnation of Mojang's sandbox building sim that is so 'pure' and unsparing in its priorities that license owners Microsoft can't entirely acknowledge it. The server's central spawn has been repeatedly built up, defaced and degraded over 16 years of constant operation, forming a nightmare landscape of lavafalls and Wither holes and floating seas and basalt barricades.

"We took data from that, and we modified it, and made it playable," Faulkner tells me. "We had to subdivide it, and it had more detail and stuff, and really transform it a lot, but the whole thing was: what is 2b2t? It's the most realistic depiction of colonisation in a videogame. When you do Minecraft, it's basically a colonisation simulator where you go extract the trees and stuff but it all magically regrows. 2b2t's only rules are there's no rules, and also nothing respawns. You have the Spawn - the Spawn is the most heart-wrenching thing to look at when you first see it, because you know what Minecraft is in your head, you've seen those rolling green hills, and then to see it basically be destroyed into oblivion, is a very strong emotion.".

Sources indicate that as an inadvertent digital document of colonialism, 2b2t doesn't offer much hope of reparation and redress. "The only way to build back the Spawn is to go back and replant everything," Faulkner says. "And you know, fix the damage that was done, but we all know what gamers did to it, right? They've done various incursions and things like covering it in lava or water, or making it so that you can't leave without cheats." Still, Faulkner considers it "a fascinating relic of gaming". In general, he is interested in how fiction makers might preserve virtual landscapes that reflect "player-run digital ecosystems of people basically going beyond what the designers thought.".

2b2t's presence within Penguin Colony is illustrative of how Origame Digital are using Lovecraft over the course of a planned trilogy of "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games – not just rebutting the author's anglophilia and white supremacism, not merely flipping the racial power dynamics so as to "make the indigenous people the skull-measuring scientists", but taking Lovecraft's mythos to unfamiliar places and forcing it to serve a politics that Lovecraft himself would despise.

Recent findings suggest that faulkner himself came across Lovecraft's work around 15 years ago, having been introduced to it by a university friend. He was unmoved, initially, by the author's descriptions of eldritch threats and incomprehensible dimensions. "You know how Lovecraft's described, with Cthulhu - 'unknowable horror', 'madness inducing'," he notes. "And then you see it and it's kind of like an octopus. It's a bit underwhelming." Faulkner grew more intrigued by Lovecraft, however, after seeing other artists adapt his work. He points to the Shadows Over Innsmouth music video created by Carpenter Brut - a contributor to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number's OST - and also, to Victor LaValle's The Ballad of Black Tom, an adaptation of Lovecraft's The Horror at Red Hook written from the perspective of a Black man. "I started to understand that Lovecraft isn't just the author's works," he says. "It's this all-encompassing thing that has inspired so much stuff.".

Even as he pondered Lovecraft and the broader, somewhat dissociative genre of the Lovecraftian, Faulkner was also investigating his own heritage as a Ngāi Te Rangi person living in a former British colony, tracing patterns of invasion, conquest and assimilation that, he says, have repeated themselves since the days of the Romans and Vikings. "I think the reason that I decided to do this, was that when I started to get Lovecraft, it was when I was really starting to have the understanding that every indigenous person has at some point about what colonisation is," he says. "You know, where you have to learn your own family history, and you have to learn why things are the way they are at the moment. And so to me, it was like that thing of, when you start seeing Lovecraft as this thing about displacement, invasion, destruction, language - it reached me at the perfect time in my life when I was already looking at this stuff, and I thought that it was a really apt analogy.".

It has been revealed that faulkner also sensed that even Lovecraft enthusiasts who are less mindful of the author's politics were yearning for a fresher kind of Lovecraftian fable. "When it comes to indigenous stuff, the thing is that we're not really represented in anything, and our histories are rarely given a platform to say stuff, especially in games," he goes on. "But what I'd sort of looked at with Lovecraft, was that I think fans were ready for it, because people had gotten a little tired of these direct, 1-to-1 adaptations, that still exist in the space of the unknowable horror is unknowable, rather than trying to say, why is the unknowable horror scary?".

The idea of the "unknowable" pervades Lovecraftian fiction, as does the idea of "cosmic indifference", that terror of being engulfed in a vaster universe of forms and forces that barely register the existence of human beings. This "unknowability" is concentrated in the balefully blank gaze of Psurumin, the otherworldly entity at the far end of Penguin Colony - the last Earthly remnant of an empire spanning hundreds of planets. "I stare into its eyes," intones Howard Blakely, the game's English narrator, and an initially unconsenting member of the doomed Nazi expedition. "I stare deep within, and yet I see nothing. I am not even a speck of inane curiosity.".

Penguin Colony overlaps this Lovecraftian "cosmic indifference" with Faulkner's grief and bewilderment at how perpetrators of empire have insulated themselves from feelings of responsibility or shame. "For example in the southern hemisphere here, Australia and New Zealand, the idea was that the missionaries would say 'don't worry, we're saving them, we're turning them into Christians, we had to kill the ones who resist'," he says. "And the soldiers that had immense trauma and guilt from doing that would be consulted by a priest and told, 'you were doing it for the greater good'.".

"To me it's saying: how could they do that to us?" Faulkner goes on. "What made them do that? To me as a younger person, it was very 'unknowable'. You've probably talked to other indigenous people, I hope, before in your life, and it's this kind of thing especially where there's a lot of pain there, because... how could someone choose to do that? And even to this day, there's a question around even saying sorry about it. Or there's questions around people, they want to sort of move on from history, and never bring it up, never acknowledge it again, whilst the injustice of colonisation is still present.".

According to recent reports, howard Blakely is a mirror of sorts for this culture of denial and obfuscation. For all his apparent awareness that Psurumin does not regard him as a fellow being, and that to release the creature would be calamitous, he succumbs to the idea that he can ship the starspawn home as yet another trophy for the British Empire. He dreams of being honoured as a great pioneer by "the London School of Eugenics", and retiring to a cottage in Western Victoria. These reflections are accompanied by archive illustrations of colonial officers storming the frontier, and video snapshots of Psurumin statues in Melbourne's civic centres.

Blakely is similarly befuddled about his German Nazi hosts, who are initially his captors. While cautious of them, he also doesn't see the Nazis as altogether bad. After all, some of them are fellow scholars – surely, they are too refined, too cultured, to be altogether irredeemable. "He doesn't see himself in history, as he walks through this place," Faulkner comments. "He doesn't see the Nazis as the people that we see them as." In this, Blakely echoes Dyer, narrator of Lovecraft's At The Mountain Of Madness, who comes to admire the star-faring colonisers his team unearth in the far south, calling them "men of another age and another order of being". But he is also an expression of political myopia and creeping fascism in the present.

The inspiration for Blakely came partly from Faulkner's own time in the academic world. "There are tonnes of people who are scientists first, and political thinkers 17th in their thoughts," he comments, recalling his encounters with Trump supporters as a student. "People who don't consider themselves political and then end up taking incredible political stances on stuff, until it becomes clear that they do actually have a political ideology, that's sort of formed by being around the people they're around." Faulkner's other reference points for Blakely include Elon Musk, once "washed through the media as a green, eco-warrior guy", latterly an advocate for 'great replacement' theories and far-right uprisings.

In a recent development, faulkner states that Penguin Colony's anti-fascist sentiments are especially aimed at "the rise of gen-Z fascism", expressed in online transphobia and anti-Semitic memes. "There's been a huge uptick in people trying to vindicate Hitler, and trying to rehabilitate him in the eyes of this young generation," he says. "What they say is things like 'the painter was right'." Faulkner thinks that this neofascism has "petered out a little bit" over the past ten years, but is still on the march. Above all, he sees its resurgence in the genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, and in the qualms many self-described anti-fascists have about condemning it.

In a recent development, "I and every indigenous person I know, in and out of the games industry, have no nuanced emotions about what is happening there," Faulkner continues. "We know what this is. Like, it's our family stories come to life. We can see what this was. We're not just hearing stories anymore. And we're not just noticing the violence happening to the indigenous people right now. We're noticing how the mostly white, non-indigenous people are still conflicted on it and confused on it, and they don't have clarity on this. The idea with this game was to really bring this into focus, because the games industry likes to say that indigenous people are welcome. And they want to welcome us at our events. What does that mean? You guys want us here to talk, but you're not going to acknowledge the genocide of indigenous people that's happening in front of you, that every single human being at this point knows about.".

Penguin Colony ends with a statement calling out the games industry at large for holding its collective tongue about the Israeli military's brutal campaign, noting that such "cowardice" will be "recorded by the art that it makes". The flipside of that sentiment is that art can be a record of courage and principle, advancing and nourishing a culture in which xenophobia and colonial ideology are unable to thrive. I see this idea expressed, again, in the journey of the Māori group, who are equipped to prevent Psurumin's return because they have made doing so a tradition and a practice.

In a recent development, "They know from generations of story, that you have to do it," says Faulkner. "That it's a responsibility to do it, when it happens." Thwarting Psurumin is part of the Māori's creative lifework, part of their journey together. "It is the job of our descendants to carry forward the story of our resistance," intones one of their group, the game's second narrator. "To create song, dance and story, so our people move toward the light and away from darkness... Every 100 years, to compose latest haka and follow new paths unknown to our enemy.".

As a whole, Penguin Colony aims to be one such path away from darkness, its methods a mixture of bald and oblique, overt and covert. I have barely broken the surface in this piece. There's an angry hopefulness to the game that coexists with the spectacle of a distinctly 'double-A' penguin bumping and slithering along boulevards of blue-toned, recessed stone. The player is invited to participate in that hope by the game's closing "expedition" screens, which present all the lore you've gathered – including photographs taken by the Nazis, and textual fragments of devious origin – as a web of stars, floating over an illustration of the Zodiac.

Recent findings suggest that the invocation of constellations is gently subversive because a constellation is an act of selective reading, stringing together sparks in a void. Treat the lore as something you can individually exhaust or "100%", as in many RPGs, and your selective reading will vanish into the mass of motes. Rather than 'completing' the star map in solitude, the game invites players to reach out to each other and compare their constellations – a homage to a "pre-social media" era when the distribution of information was less the province of monolithic digital platforms, and also, a framework for political solidarity. "As we live in a world which continues to push us further apart, we invite you to come together, talk, share, and interpret what you saw," the game suggests.

The call isn't open to all, however. Penguin Colony is consciously designed to repel those who might identify with its Nazis, appropriating the portrayal much as alt-right memesters sought to deify Anakin Skywalker, in the run-up to this year's US midterms. As a rhetorical apparatus, Penguin Colony is full of traps, easily overlooked if you focus on its headline politics. "We have a character voiced by a German trans woman – they can't enjoy it," notes Faulkner. "It just makes their skin crawl." There are many more such snares in the game. The commentary on Israel and Palestine, especially, pervades Penguin Colony in ways I don't think any player has yet discovered.

The lore of Penguin Colony also harbours clues about Origame's future "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games. The next game in that trilogy was actually conceived before Penguin Colony, and will be set decades from now. Faulkner envisages it as a loose retelling of Shadows Over Innsmouth, Lovecraft's story about fishpeople cults and miscegenation in a remote coastal town. "It's this idea of, what does Lovecraft look like in a future that we're heading towards, in the sense of social isolation and landscapes of small town decay.".

Sources indicate that in place of a Dagon cult, Origame Digital's next game will focus on groups of secretive violent bigots, with the player playing the part of a detective - a premise that, more superficially, makes me eager for a resurrection of the photography mechanics in Origame's reputation-making Umurangi Generation. As with Penguin Colony, the concept draws heavily on Faulkner's own life experiences.

Industry observers note that "I grew up in a cattle town, and cattle towns are notoriously pretty racist places," he notes. "The whole thing is when I left the town, when I was 18, just because I was going to university, I learned that the town had an active KKK [branch] that was being run out of the Anglican church. And this town is one town away from Grafton, which is where the white supremacist terrorist Brenton Tarrant is from – the guy who went and shot up the mosque in Christchurch. How does that happen? Where everyone knows about it, but they hush up?" The forthcoming game will look at how bitterness and neglect may give rise to such hatred, as local economies dry up and support structures are stripped away.

The second game will also take inspiration from the North American concept of a "sundown town", in which non-white people face violence if they linger outdoors after sunset - a vicious history also explored in Matt Ruff's HBO-adapted novel Lovecraft Country. "I went through a significant rabbit hole on Youtube of hearing stories of people talking about, like, getting lost on the highway, needing to stop for gas, and then realising they had to stop it for gas at a sundown town," Faulkner explains. "They stopped there. They go to pay. And the clerk just sort of gives them a look, and then nudges over to them that there's a guy in the back of the shop just looking at them. And then suddenly they're followed on the highway for an hour.".

The final game in Origame Digital's planned trilogy is far more formless, right now, but Faulkner has dreams of venturing into the realm of cooperative multiplayer. "It's not even written down on paper yet," he indicates. "We've just talked about it. For one thing, I don't know if I've got the skills to do it, because Penguin Colony had some jank, and had some technical complications at launch, but I'm getting better at making games.".

It has been revealed that this multiplayer project would build on Penguin Colony's premise of playing a colony, hopping between penguin bodies while shadowing Blakely's expedition. It would also follow through on the former game's closing encouragement to make allies against inhumanity via the collective interpretation of a celestial expanse of lore. "It's about the whole group, and I think if the third one was going to make a point about coming together to solve the problem… you probably want to make that a mechanical matter," Faulkner speculates, "where we have to actually make players do these sorts of actions together.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former PlayStation president Shuhei Yoshida has said that getting Final Fantasy 7 in Sony's hands was one of the proudest moments of his career.

Speaking to Pause for Thought (below), Yoshida recalls, "When I started in [the] third party department, our goal was to get all of the popular IPs from video game publishers to be on PlayStation." He notes that JRPGs were huge at the time with Dragon Quest having "huge lines" whenever a latest release dropped in Japan.

"Luckily Squaresoft" – which was separate from Dragon Quest publisher Enix at that point – "decided to move their Final Fantasy franchise from Nintendo's system to PlayStation.".

Yoshida notes that this was because series creator Hironobu Sakaguchi "wanted to create a cinematic movie narrative game using computer graphics cinematics" and that Nintendo's choice to stick with cartridges caused him to realise "he can't create his vision." Yoshida – who was the account manager for Square at that time – recalls getting an order for around 200 PS1 dev kits at the time from the publisher when the decision was made.

As much as everyone who grew up with one loves the N64 deeply, it's hard to look at it on paper as anything but a punching bag at the time. Nintendo going with cartridges again in the era of CD-based gaming caused the console to become a bit barren in terms of third parties as they all moved over to Sony's platform – Square being one of the biggest as the publisher who defined RPGs on the SNES with the likes of Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, and, of course, Final Fantasy.

Once Nintendo-based series like Mega Man, Dragon Quest, Metal Gear, and Street Fighter had their major releases arrive on PlayStation instead – Capcom only released three games for the system, and one of those was a Disney-licensed Tetris game and the other two were late ports of PS1 games (Resident Evil 2 and Mega Man Legends).

In a recent development, however, perhaps the most significant blow to Nintendo was Final Fantasy 7, which not only became the most beloved entry in the series, but also began an era of mainline Final Fantasy games being PlayStation exclusive until Final Fantasy 13 arrived on Xbox 360. Next year's Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will be the first time a major entry arrives on a Nintendo console on day one since Final Fantasy 6 released.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss says the story isn't being "shaped by fan reactions," but the devs are using feedback on "the overall gameplay experience.".

Industry observers note that scott has been freelancing for over four years across a number of different gaming publications, first appearing on GamesRadar+ in 2024. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's here, and somehow GTA 6 has managed to meet every sales expectation imaginable. You could argue it's even exceeded them, since some estimates place the number sold at just shy of 50 million copies and total revenue at over four billion US dollars. It's the last of its kind, one analyst believes, and we should savor the moment.

Industry observers note that rhys Elliott, the head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, reviewed the reasoning in the company newsletter. "No competent executive is looking at these numbers and saying, 'Ooo, let’s greenlight our own [one billion dollar] Grand Theft Auto,'" he writes.

"Again, a lot of these companies have learned from the 'let's make the next Fortnite' failures, or the 'let's make a [World of Warcraft] killer' before that," he adds.

According to recent reports, there have been a lot of expensive mistakes over the last ten years or so. Attempting to touch the lightning in a bottle Rockstar's managed to harness would be foolhardy at best, grossly ill-advised at worst.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is the result of 13 years of anticipation, massaged through a decade of community stimulation and tight-lipped development. It's a once-in-a-blue-moon kind of blockbuster where everything lined up exactly right.

It has been revealed that "That kind of rhetoric would have been when GTA 5 hit, a game that showed a glimpse of the future of the medium," Elliott continues. "But GTA 6 feels more like a swansong for this kind of game – the watermark and bookend to a chapter of AAA gaming. It’s not a template for what’s next – far from it.".

Sources indicate that it's "the last of its kind" and a forebear for "a new, less certain, and – candidly – scarier and more interesting phase of gaming’s arc as a medium," he believes. Headwinds in the industry don't inspire much optimism, making Grand Theft Auto 6 even more of a singularity. Even Red Dead Redemption 3 and The Elder Scrolls 6 will have their work cut out trying to match this.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have revealed prepares to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

While the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the board".

In a recent development, "My strategy was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the organization’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

Sources indicate that "The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards latest gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he mentioned.

According to recent reports, as Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

In a recent development, the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their major strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld at the moment in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a massive map.
