📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upcoming multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

According to recent reports, there's nothing forcing you to do any of this in company, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

In a recent development, I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

Spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

Recent findings suggest that spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit.

You can read more about the game on Steam. I find Spirit Crossing quite novel, especially when it dispenses with the WholeCosy "discover your inner fashonista" stuff and leans into the supernatural elements: I like the idea of hunkering by the campfire during a storm, watching the clouds hurtle past. Still, I'm disappointed to hear that Spry Fox have made use of generative AI during its creation.

According to recent reports, as has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, the developers called on Anthropic's Claude tools for various behind-the-scenes tasks - the example they give in a Discord post is editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

Industry observers note that it's hardly a full-throated endorsement of generative AI, but it still forms part of a political and cultural project I consider reckless and morbid. For a longer account of my objections, albeit one that doesn't cover Claude in particular, here's my longform thinkywangle from July last year.

#166295. Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1512 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games.
  • It has been revealed that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95.
  • Microsoft, all the while, were taking notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.

It has been revealed that unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95. At E3 later that May, Microsoft demonstrated the Strategic Commander for the first time with SimCity 3000, while promoting its potential for other such games as Diablo II, Warcraft III, and Baldur's Gate II. This was all taking place during the so-called 'Golden Age of Real-Time Strategy Games,' which spanned roughly from the mid-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was when the RTS genre was at the peak of its mainstream popularity, and we fans were devoted to mastering its intricacies in any way we could to have a competitive edge.

Microsoft, all the while, were taking notes. "The team conceived the Strategic Commander in the late 1990s," Carl Ledbetter - then Industrial Design Manager for Microsoft's PC Hardware Group, now Head of Design for Xbox Devices - recalls to me. "As RTS games grew in popularity, we saw an interesting opportunity to design a new physical interface around a new interaction model. The idea was for it to be used left-handed in concert with right-hand PC desktop mouse control. We wanted to enable players to perform faster with more fluidity, comfort, optimised control placement for multiple hand sizes, simplicity of set-up, and ease of programming.".

In a recent development, for Ledbetter and co. to realise this ambition, the Strategic Commander was designed as a unique combination of mouse, joystick, and gamepad. To manage the increasing complexities of the RTS games of the day, it came equipped with six programmable buttons, three shift buttons, and a three-position profile switch. Back then, these atypical features provided an unprecedented 72 possible key combinations across various configurations, all at the tip of our stubby little fingers. Better yet, it allowed us to toggle between three pre-configured profiles at a time, so that we could switch up our configurations on the fly depending on which stage of an RTS match we were in.

On release, contemporary reviewers acknowledged its originality, with critics like ActiveWin's Julien Jay describing it as "probably the most innovative (with the GameVoice) and revolutionary" peripheral designed specifically for strategy players. Others, like Neoseeker's Arnel Lim, suggested that it might’ve gone overboard with its customisation options, saying "you won't use anywhere close to all of them," in reference to the controller's programmable key combinations. Either way, the Strategic Commander failed to supplant conventional peripherals in the hands of most RTS players, and it was discontinued in 2003. As was the rest of the original SideWinder line, owing to declining sales and the industry-wide shift toward standard M+K setups for all PC games and genres.

However, unlike so many of its Microsoft-made siblings, this was not the end for the Strategic Commander. Niche as it was, it went on to enjoy a surprisingly long post-shelf life, one that was stretched out by a dedicated cult following - and that continues to this day. But why? Why, after all these years, is this forgotten peripheral from a discontinued line maintaining such a enthusiastic fanbase, years after the industry around it had written it off as a failure?

According to recent reports, the answer lies in software and OS compatibility, as much as the hardware's own appeal. Andreas Weis was the developer of one of the first unofficial patches for the Strategic Commander, allowing players to keep on using it even after the original software stopped being compatible with newer versions the Windows. By that point, the device was a decade old, and well into 'official' obsolescence, yet Weis still answered the call of the Strategic Commander's righteously frustrated - if numerically few - fans. "There was a lot of interest back in the early 2010s in software patches to keep the Strategic Commander functional when the original software for the Strategic Commander stopped working," he explains. "Users were asking around on internet forums about how to get it to work on Windows 7 and Vista machines. Since I was studying computer science at the time, I was quite interested in reverse-engineering, and I hacked together a simple tool that would cover my use cases for the device.".

In the years that followed, other patches were released to keep the Strategic Commander operational, the most notable of which was Philip Merwarth’s Strategic Engine software in 2013. Unfortunately, they weren’t open-source. Worse was that the protocol for programming the Strategic Commander wasn’t documented anywhere online in a way that was accessible for people. This is why Weis realized that he could make a unique contribution.

In a recent development, "I polished my old prototype code for the Strategic Commander software patch and released it as a library, so that other people could use it to write their own applications for programming the tool," he says. "As for me, I released one application that made use of the library publicly, the vJoy feeder application, which allows the device to be used with games that support joystick inputs." Curiously, Weis, by this time and like many others, had found other applications for a device with such a specific selling point, and even continues to use the Strategic Commander sparingly in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that "The production quality of Microsoft hardware at the time was just top-notch, and I love the design of the old SideWinder devices, which is why I did not just throw the thing out when the software stopped working," he tells me. "It was worth keeping around to find new uses for it over the years, and I eventually realized that it makes quite a nice addition to a HOTAS (Hands-On Throttle And Stick) setup, where I could put actions that aren’t time-critical and don't fit well on the throttle on the Strategic Commander instead. For example, when I’m playing Elite Dangerous in VR, I’d put actions like deploying the landing gear on the Strategic Commander to free up buttons on the throttle for actions that were more relevant for combat.".

Sources indicate that when looking back at the history of Microsoft’s SideWinder line, it’s easy to call the Strategic Commander a failed experiment, given the fact that most of us are still using the same standard mouse-and-keyboard setup to play RTS games. However, the central premise behind its design philosophy was that the interface between a player and a game could be redesigned to cater to specific genre quirks, and decades following its release, it’s still maintained a coalition of loyal users: some RTS players who believed the Strategic Commander really pulled it off, and those found other uses for the device in other flavours of PC game. And with the matter of modern compatibility, a roadblock for so much retro hardware, bypassed by homemade patches, both camps can continue twisting and clicking their Strategic Commanders unimpeded.

All the same, I wonder if it might have basked in more conventional success, had Microsoft made more forward-thinking decisions. The Strategic Commander has proven over the years that its unprecedented customisation had applications far beyond what Ledbetter’s team had envisioned, and once the popularity of RTS games settled down, other, similar click-heavy subgenres like MOBAs and Real-Time Tactics got big as well. Would a more officially maintained, potentially refined Strategic Commander model have served those crowds? I think it might. The narrow focus on RTS games may have also hurt the device's since-demonstrated broader appeal; if Microsoft had fully capitalised on this customisation selling point by communicating its benefits to everyone, not just those playing the single most popular PC genre at the time, it could have provided the blueprint for a proper, long-lived alternative to controllers, mice, and keyboards.

According to recent reports, alas, gaming history is littered with revolutionary peripherals that failed to actually revolutionise the industry surrounding them. The Strategic Commander is no different, but for the fact that it’s had this surprisingly long post-shelf life - and, as a result, the opportunity for insight into what could have been done to salvage the its failures. Still, that unexpected longevity can provide come comfort to the Strategic Commander's creators, as well as its lingering customers.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the design made sense for its time, especially with the rising popularity of RTS games," Ledbetter reflects. "Looking back, I would have liked more time to test and refine the Strategic Commander. I’m proud of what we brought to market, and I’m glad to know that it remains beloved by many players to this day.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

In a recent development, "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers.".

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

Recent findings suggest that so, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

It has been revealed that if you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later declared that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

Sources indicate that this isn't the first substantial bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a upcoming mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Early on in GTA 6, you'll gain access to the JoySystem, a game console with a handful of games you can play. One of those is Tenebrae Lux, a black and white, first-person puzzle game. In this GTA 6 guide, we have a Tenebrae Lux walkthrough, guiding you through the puzzles to reach the ending.

Tenebrae Lux features randomised elements in some of its puzzles, so your experience may vary from what you see in our images and videos.

Below is our walkthrough of Tenebrae Lux, revealing puzzle solutions and where to find notes.

There are 11 notes to collect in total, but the last two require you to collect the previous nine.

It has been revealed that in a single playthrough of Tenebrae Lux, you can find those 9 notes hidden in 17 possible locations. Collecting these 9 notes will then allow you to find the 10th and 11th notes.

After waking up on the island, you must solve at least three grid-based puzzles located on the beach, though there are five to find in total — two of which are necessary if you're looking for every note.

Go inside the shelter and head for the wooden boxes directly opposite the entrance:.

On the table you'll find Note Location #1, as pictured:.

As is the case with all the other Board Puzzles, Board Puzzle #1 is randomly selected from a batch of puzzles; you won't always be presented with the same one.

To solve the puzzle, follow the steps in the below videos depending on which puzzle you have in front of you:.

After checking Note Location #2, enter the shelter to the right. This is what it looks like:.

Head towards the wooden crate at the back-right part of the building:.

Here are the possible solutions we've found so far:.

After solving Board Puzzle #3, turn around and leave the shack through the door ahead:.

Turn right and inspect the railing; this is Note Location #4, where you may find a note on the railing:.

After checking Note Location #4, go around to the front of the shack, where you entered the first time:.

To the right of the entrance are a couple of crates; this is Note Location #5, where you may find a note resting against the crates:.

After solving Board Puzzle #3, exit the shelter and go left along the coast (it's quite a walk):.

You'll come to a room with several things you must pay attention to in order to solve this next puzzle. You'll need to make some notes!

The goal is to input the correct string of numbers into the telephone on the back wall. However, there is no defined phone number for you to use; it is a randomised solution.

To learn the phone number, you must pass through several incarnations of the same room to discover differences in the environment, one by one.

Upon first entering the room, you'll see the text "DEVELOPED USING ZUCHWORKS ENGINE" followed by a Greek letter:.

Sources indicate that this puzzle is also somewhat randomised, but use these examples to help. Again, this is just about using the door that's furthest from the other people:.

You'll need to do this a number of times, eventually leading to a final cutscene and the game's first ending:.

Tenebrae Lux contains 2 possible endings.

You will get the first ending by just completing the game normally:.

The second ending requires much more for you to complete:.

Sources indicate that to begin playing Tenebrae Lux, you must progress enough to unlock the JoySystem console. This occurs in Chapter 1 during the mission Feng Shui.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arion Kurtaj, the now 21-year-old hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022, has been released from prison, as a judge warns that he shouldn't try this kind of hack again.

Kurtaj was 16 years old when his hacks against Rockstar began alongside other members of hacking group Lapsus$. Following the release of at least 90 videos featuring early GTA 6 gameplay, Kurtaj was deemed psychiatrically unfit for trial and was eventually sentenced to a lifetime stay in a secure hospital because of his severe autism. Rockstar noted that the hack had cost it $5 million.

But Kurtaj's status changed in January, when he was transferred to a standard prison ahead of a planned retrial. Last week, he pleaded guilty to hacks against Rockstar and others.

According to recent reports, kurtaj has been given a seven-year sentence and released on the same day, as the BBC reports. He had already served the majority of that sentence during his time in the secure hospital and prison. The judge, Mr. Justice Turner, told Kurtaj "you are a very talented young man," but offered a warning: "Don't let this happen again.".

Sources indicate that the hacker has been released on license which, for my fellow Americans, is essentially a form of parole. He's been given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting him from using online services including Telegram and Discord.

Of course, this isn't the only hacking incident Rockstar is dealing with. Ahead of launch, a hacking group or individual known as Cyberleek released numerous gameplay videos from a seemingly near-final build of GTA 6. Now, Cyberleek has released an Xbox build of the game which modders are working to turn into a full-blown PC port. At this point, it's possible that an unofficial GTA 6 PC port could land before Rockstar can deliver an official version.

GTA 6 patch gives players losing progress to crashes a lifeline – and it looks like the first-person and 60fps glitches are safe for now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
  • The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year.
  • The trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

The trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

"But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

You know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which presently looks likely to last until at least 2028.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic.
  • This newly introduced mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on.
  • In a recent development, as for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star.

Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

This newly introduced mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

In a recent development, as for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an problem for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming upgrade, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tasha Suri, author of the Burning Kingdoms trilogy and several other books, will be writing Baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart, the official BG3books website has declared. Another prequel to Larian's videogame, this one focuses on Shadowheart's time as a priestess in the Church of Shar, and is about a murder mystery.

"When a member of their order is killed in the Upper City," the blurb goes, "Shadowheart and her so-called allies are called to investigate. She trusts none of them: not Mirie, the ambitious Griefguard; not Caldan, the cynical propagandist; and certainly not Nocturne, the charming quartermistress, who claims to have only Shadowheart’s best interests in mind.".

Mirie and Nocturne are both characters you can meet in Baldur's Gate 3, while Caldan Darkwood is mentioned in a note you can find. Nocturne in particular has a close relationship with Shadowheart, which could be interesting to see developed. "Torn between the familiar comforts of the dark and the thrill of upcoming desire," the blurb continues, "she must solve the mystery to prove her devotion… or be cast into the light.".

Which sounds fine and dandy, but it'll have an uphill battle with the Baldur's Gate 3 fandom, who've been vocally critical of the Astarion novel for its lightness of tone—especially given his traumatic backstory—and apparently mischaracterizing Astarion and his sire, Cazador, as well as being inaccurate to the lore.

Sources indicate that I haven't read the Astarion book, but I did read the original Baldur's Gate novels, which were terrible. So were almost all the D&D books I read in a youthful post-Tolkien haze where I'd put up with anything that had wizards in it. My expectations are pretty low, but I do like to slip a trashy fantasy novel between heavier reads as a palate-cleanser so maybe I'll try this one some day.

Baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart will be out in a 304-page hardcover edition and in ebook form on June 8, as well as a 10-hour audiobook. The Astarion audiobook was read by Astarion performer Neil Newbon, we'll have to wait and see if Jennifer English reads the Shadowheart book.

If the series continues I could see a Wyll prequel being interesting, since he gets a bit short-changed in the videogame, though I wouldn't expect it to sell as well as novels about the more popular companions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole latest world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

Sources indicate that on occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators stated in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it.".

Recent findings suggest that they aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

Recent findings suggest that "Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month.".

It has been revealed that the battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both vital to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later update for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

It has been revealed that woW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of new quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

In a recent development, it makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

Recent findings suggest that thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

It's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

In terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock new rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Sources indicate that between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make new, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Sources indicate that every latest Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

Recent findings suggest that "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch noted in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

According to recent reports, while Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

If you'd like to reminisce a bit before the long-awaited game finally hits, you can check out our favourite Grand Theft Auto pieces Eurogamer's published over the years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I have been inundated with GTA 6-related advertising over the last few weeks. Every company on the planet has been in my inbox with some kind of press release tying their product to this massive fresh release - just this morning I was emailed by a bedding company about all the hours of sleep people must have missed out on in order to pull all-nighters in Leonida. But perhaps the most interesting tie-in comes from Pavel Durov, founder and CEO of messaging service Telegram.

Sources indicate that telegram, if you're not aware, is a messaging platform that is best known for its security, driven by end-to-end encryption and self-destructing messages that make it pretty good for keeping information secret. This makes it pretty popular with, say, investigative journalists, but has also given Telegram a bit of a reputation as something that's also a bit handy if you're a career criminal looking to keep people off your trail. Of course, that particular reputation is not something the company's founder and CEO would be keen to lean into. Or so you might think...

Late last night, Durov tweeted that "the least realistic thing about GTA 6 is that Jason and Lucia run a whole criminal operation without a single Telegram group." Now, I get it. I get the desire to seem like you're part of the zeitgeist, like you're linked to this major new cultural touchstone, and to organically tie your product into that conversation. What I don't entirely get is the impulse to say the quiet part out loud.

The least realistic thing about GTA VI is that Jason and Lucia run a whole criminal operation without a single Telegram group.November 22, 2026.

In a recent development, if I know that Telegram is probably pretty useful if you want to keep your illicit dealings secret, Durov must definitely know that. However, Durov also has a product to sell and (presumably) a reputation to uphold as a fine, upstanding citizen who definitely isn't making criminals' lives easier. Put aside for now the fact that GTA 6 has a dedicated 'steal this car' app, and I might avoid making the link between the game and my app so explicitly about crime. Especially given that GTA makes up its own parody software companies to ape those in the real world, and you'd think Durov might have decided to sit this one out.

Recent findings suggest that unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that plan release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental complications.

Recent findings suggest that unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

Recent findings suggest that the grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

Sources indicate that the GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

Industry observers note that at the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

Sources indicate that as the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

Sources indicate that "We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar noted at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way.".

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

The manifesto states that "GenAI is at the moment harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

The effects of the technology on gamemakers, such as "directly and indirectly replacing workers", "worker fatigue, cognitive decline and burnout", and "a marked decline in junior positions in the industry" are listed as core harms to be avoided and fought against, with the manifesto also noting that it also "removes a sense of ownership from workers [...] the things they produce no longer feel like they have the workers' stamp on them, and therefore they can no longer take pride in them." As it states, "games are best made by people.".

The manifesto goes on to explains the unions' stance that genAI is "sold to employers as an alternative to workers", and its "predisposition towards sycophancy and lack of real world context can lead to an increase in unreasonable, damaging requests when used by employers to set policy, timescales, workloads, etc., as well as to task expansion and a general degradation of conditions." In addition, its nature as a tool built on the theft of stolen third-party data is highlighted as an inherent danger, and the so-called loophole in only training models on internal data is equally highlighted as resulting in employees and creators rarely being credited or compensated for their work that is fed into the machine. This glitch also ties into the inherent implicit and explicit discrimination that exists in genAI content due to datasets' "intrinsic and exclusionary Western bias that limits diversity and marginalises non-dominant languages, cultures, and ethnicities", which leads to "a homogenisation of culture.".

Recent findings suggest that as for action, the manifest recommends that workers should "avoid usage of genAI services whenever possible", "distance yourself from genAI usage", and "make it clear to your employer why you do not want to use genAI", as well as, of course, to "organise. Unionise. Do it now, not when it is too late and you are already under threat." Similarly, employers are recommended to "ensure that no worker is required to use genAI", and to "disallow the use of genAI in the company code of conduct, even for early stages of development." Finally, for consumers, it simply advises to "support games made without genAI", and to "be vocal about disliking genAI in games.".

In a recent development, it's an incredibly clear and concise statement that calls to mind the statement made by a selection of IGF jurors on the state of genAI in the industry and their decision not to vote for any game that uses genAI in any capacity. As both of these statements are joined in saying, "we do not have to accept the use of genAI to make video games; it is not inevitable.".

A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand newly introduced mode, Free Play, to Star Wars: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.".

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.

Galactic Racer already has a pretty good selection of online multiplayer modes, like the 12-player speeder races and 8-player podracing tours, but there's at the moment no way to play with your mates in the same room.

Industry observers note that chris Donlan loved the thrilling racing game for mixing the best bits of Star Wars and Burnout - Fuse Games does have plenty of old Criterion DNA, mind you. "It's latest games, with Roguelite choices and endless unlockables, and it's also old games, with cruel and ingenious courses where everything can be lost in an instant. It's a Galaxy Far, Far Away, and it's also Paradise City," he wrote in Eurogamer's five-star review.

In a recent development, with Galactic Racer and Zero Company under its belt, Lucasfilm Games stated it's now "more flexible" about which developers it accepts pitches from. Hopefully, that'll lead to even more interesting games set in Star Wars' ultra flexible world.

Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion.

One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life.

In a recent development, "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

Sources indicate that humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6, Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained.

It has been revealed that establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's crucial is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world.".

This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts. And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does.

I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1273 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again.
  • It has been revealed that tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did.
  • For Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.

It has been revealed that tonally and in terms of setting, Sleeping Dogs feels a lot closer to GTA 4’s gritty urban gangland drama than Rockstar’s follow-up did. GTA 5 is an exotic and sun-kissed heist movie, a mould that GTA 6’s tale of gun-toting love in Vice City very much looks to follow. That leaves Sleeping Dogs protagonist Wei Shen standing next to Niko Bellic. One might be kicking faces in Hong Kong and the other might be getting into shootouts in New York, but both are fresh off the boat in places both familiar and alien. They find themselves caught between two lives.

For Wei, it’s a balancing act between his day-to-day life surviving among the triads, and keeping his hands clean while securing evidence against them as an undercover cop. For Niko, it’s a balancing act between trying to settle old scores and start a fresh life in post 9/11 America. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a pork bun to chow down on. One can stop at a street vendor to buy a hotdog to chow down on. Both of their games are beloved for delivering tales which get the player invested in Wei and Niko specifically, that excel in putting you into the emotional shoes of these two underworld operators whose worlds are tearing at them from multiple angles as they claw their way to the top of the food chain.

Despite my headline gag, they do this with a comparably minimal amount of in-depth life-simmy details, like those that’re baked into Red Dead Redemption 2 (and GTA 6, to a degree) as some of the main selling points. Wei can buy a pork bun, the vendor loudly informs him that by doing so he’s avoiding the possibility of never becoming a whole man, but there’s no ‘whole manliness’ meter which demands to be satiated with regular pork bun munching, lest Wei become a less than whole man. All it does is give him a temporary health regeneration boost, because as we all know, the first thing the doctors do if you’re admitted to hospital with grievous wounds after a fight is serve you a scrumptious meal that miraculously closes up your cuts in minutes.

Sleeping Dogs dedicates all of its life simming effort to making you feel the weight of Wei’s torment as he grapples with an unsustainable double life of sinning and saintly acts. Like GTA 4, it’s not got the time, tech, or budget to adorn itself with animations or systems that replicate every aspect of Wei’s day-to-day existence in excruciating detail. It’s simply assumed, rather than demonstrated, that some of the back alleys he wanders down to bust drug dealers probably smell a bit unpleasant. He doesn’t have over 60 species of bird to catalogue as he commutes from North Point to the businessman-infested Central district, then on to the houseboat-heavy Aberdeen and gated communities of Kennedy Town. Though, he does keep nicking jade statues, in order to persuade his kung fu instructor to teach him some fun latest ways to knee baddies into submission.

He can sing his lungs out to nail I Fought the Law at one of Hong Kong’s few karaoke booths or lose all of his cash playing mahjong, but he doesn’t have an endless laundry list of optional hobbies long enough to suck players who aren’t even particularly trying to get distracted in for hundreds of hours.

Industry observers note that then again, if he wanders into his Central apartment, Wei can take a piss. In truth, I’d forgotten about this prior to my recent revisit, but it is a wonderfully simple feature that really emphasises how things’ve changed for games like these in the years since 2012. I press one button when the prompt pops up near the loo, and Wei unzips before dribbling a rather loud trickle into the bowl. Then, he’s done. I can get him to wash his hands if I wish, but no bladder meter has gone down and no dirtiness meter is being satiated by my scrubbing. If Wei doesn’t take regular whizzes, no NPCs comment that he’s looking a bit pained, and his walking animation doesn’t dynamically adjust to huddle his legs closer together.

You could ask what was even the point of animating Wei’s pissing if it’s a pointless and totally optional activity, outside of arguably doing a tiny bit of work in helping Shen be convincingly human (and it unquestionably being quite funny the first time you stumble across it). By looping what would once have been one-note button presses into systems that help them play a more active role in fleshing out the world and the routines of its inhabitants, uber-detailed games like GTA 6 - at their best - add an extra layer of definition to the tales and adventures they depict.

They often feel like the sort of game Sleeping Dogs might’ve been if it’d had their tech and its budget was the GDP of real world Hong Kong. The question is, when limitations like that don’t apply to the degree they once did, where the line lies between extra layers which tangibly deepen the player’s experience and overindulgent bloat?

Sleeping Dogs, despite working in its own takes on elements of GTA, Saints Row, and I’d argue RGG Studio’s earlier Like A Dragon/Yakuza entries, is an unquestionably lean and focused game. Less isn’t necessarily more, especially if you were to ask slumbering canines-loving teenage me, who would’ve bitten your hand off for Hong Kong to boast even a third of the extra features and activities GTA 6 and Red Dead 2 pack into their life of crime sims.

It has been revealed that the latter two are games that wouldn’t have been possible to make, at least in a format the masses would be able to play, back in the era when Sleeping Dogs and GTA 4 represented what an open-world crime game typically looked like. They’ve eaten up what used to be the domain of arcade racers like Midnight Club and hunting sims to step closer to being something reminiscent of Better Than Life, the addictive VR everything game from the Red Dwarfverse, which takes over players’ lives by simulating a world where everything they want can play out in reality-mimicking detail.

They aim to be far, far more than what defined their predecessors, and to use that to appeal to an ever-expanding audience. What I’m intrigued to see, whenever I get my hands on Rockstar’s latest work, is whether those like me who come to it having recently played a game like Sleeping Dogs will find a game that feels like it’s being pulled in a million different directions, to the point that it loses something of what historically has been at the centre of its fundamental appeal.

Or, to put it another way: is there a point at which you’ve eaten so many pork buns in one sitting that you begin to stray away from the self-actualisation which steady consumption of them is known to facilitate?

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Assuming you didn't just buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S to play Grand Theft Auto 6, your console's limited storage space is likely already strained, meaning tough choices may have to be made to make room for Rockstar's chonky 212GB crime game.

Recent findings suggest that in a move I don't remember seeing before, EA is asking players to spare Madden NFL 27 from the purge to free up console storage space. As spotted by Push Square, a desperate in-game message pops up when you launch the American Football game, pleading with you not to delete it.

The message highlights 17th November as the date of a Madden NFL 27 enhancement, though its styling, wording and choice of background seem to hint at GTA 6.

According to recent reports, "Don't delete!" it reads, as shared by Zirksee on X. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission.".

EA's language and intention, however, are much clearer in this post on X, which specifically references GTA 6's large file size in a cheeky way, seemingly promoting the same enhancement.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

Recent findings suggest that the update in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

As part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. That includes EA Sports, of course, where a team is at the moment developing a game codenamed Project Gridiron, described as "a social-first open-world experience for our American Football team".

Sony has shared a selection of staggering statistics relating to the launch of GTA 6 on PS5.

From launch on 19th November through to the end of the title's opening weekend, Sony recorded over 39 million unique players.

The game set a newly introduced record on PlayStation for the highest number of concurrent players on any game.

PS5 players have logged 683 million hours of GTA 6 playtime, and on average, every owner on PlayStation has played it for 17.4 hours.

Recent findings suggest that outside of the console's launch and Christmas holidays, the launch of GTA 6 resulted in "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day". GTA 6 was the first game played on 70% of those latest PS5 systems.

It has been revealed that the day after release, Rockstar Games announced GTA 6 had sold 32.5 million units across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. With these latest stats from PlayStation, we know it's sold over 39 million copies on PS5 alone, as of yesterday.

GTA 6 will continue to sell for years to come, as there'll be a PC version next year along with a brand newly introduced iteration of GTA Online. We've got a 10/10-rated GTA 6 PS5 review on the site, and we're working on our comprehensive GTA 6 guide right now.

World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.
  • This exploit was quickly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a right now-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits.
  • Industry observers note that this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

This exploit was quickly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a right now-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

Industry observers note that this was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

According to recent reports, for an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Recent findings suggest that looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point.".

Flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream notes enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked.".

Industry observers note that you may be wondering why this is such a big deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

According to recent reports, the counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

According to recent reports, as of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the massive question.

Recent findings suggest that gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher Fresh Blood Interactive's latest revision post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by New Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Other than these fresh hires, the update is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

In a recent development, the update is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but Upcoming Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah states poor management from EA led to BioWare's was shutdown.

Mass Effect and Dragon Age maker BioWare was shut down by EA shortly after the publisher was acquired by a group of private investors. The studio – while beloved for its legendary RPGs across a 30-year history – had faced a ton of issues over its final few years with high-profile titles like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard failing to impress fans. Some pointed fingers at the studio itself for its demise.

Speaking to Pembridge (via PC Gamer) Darrah recalls an unnamed person's read on the situation: "EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself.".

He adds, "they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it,'" in regards to EA's approach to BioWare.

In a recent development, "The reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this,'" Darrah explains, "but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options.".

He points to BioWare's pivot to the Frostbite engine, Dragon Age 2's breakneck development cycle, and the whole situation with Anthem as things that were brought about by pressure from EA.

It has been revealed that "They basically remarked [you] got to hit your financials. So what are you going to do?" Darrah adds, "Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes.
  • And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

In a recent development, sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

The enhancement should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly stated so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Industry observers note that any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.
